intro: Iran’s past unfolds through archaeological landscapes, changing dynasties and everyday social experience. Follow the connections between ancient settlements, modern political transformations and the people who shaped them.
Culture lives in conversation, shared meals and the things people make. Languages, celebrations and regional traditions reveal many ways of belonging within Iran.
Mountains, inland basins and contrasting coastlines give Iran a varied physical character. Water, vegetation and settlement connect these landscapes with the experience of living in them.
Economic development brings resources, productive skills and infrastructure into changing relationships. Look across industries to see the systems behind everyday goods and services.
Learning takes place in schools, universities, workshops and research laboratories. Institutions and individual ambitions connect education with the wider life of society.
Business opportunities emerge where useful skills meet practical needs. Explore the technologies, teams and support networks behind Iran’s changing landscape of enterprise.
Travel can begin with curiosity about a place rather than a fixed itinerary. Cities, rural communities and cultural landscapes offer different invitations to look closer.

Public institutions organize authority and the delivery of shared responsibilities. This guide introduces their roles and relationships through neutral explanations of government, representation and civic life.
Creative expression moves between inherited forms and individual experiments. Music, cinema, literature and visual art reveal different ways of interpreting Iranian experience.
Social change becomes visible through households, mobility and the organization of work. Different communities experience these transformations in different ways.
Health connects professional care with the conditions of everyday life. Explore institutions, technologies and research fields through general explanations rather than individual medical advice.
Environmental questions connect natural systems with human choices. Water, energy and material use reveal the practical work behind sustainability and conservation.
Sport brings people together through movement, competition and shared attention. Traditional practices and digital play add different dimensions to recreation and community life.
Media shapes how information is made, circulated and understood. Follow the people, formats and infrastructure connecting a story with its audience.
Digital experiences depend on physical networks and carefully coordinated software. Infrastructure connects advanced technical capabilities with the services people use every day.
Food systems begin with living landscapes and continue through storage, processing and exchange. Agriculture connects practical knowledge with the stewardship of land and water.
Materials move from geological resources into the built and manufactured world. Extraction, processing and recovery reveal different stages of that industrial journey.
Public infrastructure supports movement and the routines of settlement. Roads, utilities and shared spaces connect individual households with the wider city.
Financial institutions connect payments, savings and the allocation of resources. Understand their different roles without treating general information as an investment recommendation.
Business institutions create frameworks for exchange, organization and innovation. This introduction explains their purposes while keeping general orientation separate from legal advice.
Scientific heritage survives in texts, instruments and structures that solved practical problems. Looking at how knowledge was made and used connects intellectual history with skilled work.
Creative industries connect cultural expression with the work of making a living. Design, publishing and performance depend on production systems as well as individual imagination.
Domestic markets connect household needs with goods, services and distribution. Everyday purchasing reveals relationships between taste, access and productive activity.
Iran’s regions offer distinct combinations of settlement, landscape and local memory. Explore cities and provinces as living places rather than collections of isolated landmarks.
Statistics can clarify a question when their definitions and limits are understood. This guide explains what different datasets describe without inventing current figures.
Iran’s international connections take shape through trade, knowledge and cultural exchange. Regional routes and diaspora communities add human relationships to the map of cooperation.
